Deel, a global HR and payroll platform operating 24/7 support across chat, email, and phone in over 150 countries, needed more than just a support QA solution. They needed a platform that would allow them to build a scalable, best-in-class quality assurance and agent training program that would enable their teams to move at the highest speed and service quality in the market.

By implementing Intryc's AI-driven platform, the Operational Excellence team at Deel has more than doubled their evaluation output, at a fraction of the time previously required and with the same QA headcount, while almost eliminating all previous manual work and improving root cause targeting accuracy.

The platform they were using before Intryc had limitations. Managing multiple scorecards made trend analysis difficult, and the manual QA process consumed significant time on tasks that didn't contribute to insight generation. As Portillo explains: "Not having better QA coverage limited our visibility into performance trends and slowed down coaching cycles."

Deel evaluated several top QA platforms using G2 reviews and peer recommendations. "We noticed that a lot of them had good QA processes, appeared to be very strong, but they lacked the flexibility that we needed as we were trying to scale," Portillo says. Most platforms fell short on key dimensions: customization required extra manual effort, and data centralization was limited.

"Automation reduced manual work in assigning tickets and reporting, allowing QAs to focus on insights and process improvements. We now have a data-driven approach to evaluate performance and reward our teams" (Portillo).

Automation features now save several hours per week per QA analyst. QA analysts at Deel have elevated their scope of work, instead focusing on core issues or patterns across the business that need the most attention from support or adjacent teams like product, engineering, or sales. Evaluations move faster and provide more thorough, detailed insights.

Tagging accuracy and process consistency both improved, contributing to faster First Contact Resolution and more relevant coaching sessions. "While CSAT and NPS are influenced by many factors, the improved QA visibility and feedback cycles have supported a noticeable improvement in overall agent performance and quality consistency across teams" (Portillo).
